provider: EVEO Object Storage S3 (Brazil) — the only zero-egress S3 endpoint found in Latin America

free_tier.stated: R$0.05/GB/month, billed on stored GB only; buckets up to 5 PB, no provisioning. Positioned as «Armazenamento sem taxas de download (egress) ou API».
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: ZERO, stated as the product's entire pitch: «Zero Egress e API … a saída é gratuita, operações PUT, GET, LIST não pesam na fatura» (egress is free; PUT/GET/LIST operations do not weigh on the invoice). Also «paga apenas pelo GB armazenado … e acessa o que é seu sem taxas de pedágio». No retrieval fee. WORM immutability native.

tooling: S3-compatible with SigV4 presigned URLs. So it can sit behind Cloudflare the same way as any S3 store. rclone `s3`, restic, Veeam. Two-region replication inside Brazil, Tier III datacentres.
chaining: Pure per-GB, so 5 TB and 20 TB cost the same per TB. No bucket cap below 5 PB.
limits_note: Brazil-only geography. The same intercontinental-latency objection as Rollin Host for the hot set, though as an archive tier it is fine. The R$0.05/GB figure is the advertised rate and no volume staircase is published, so there may be no discount at 20 TB; ask. Enterprise sales motion («Simule seu Storage», «Solicite uma proposta») rather than self-serve checkout.
reliability_note: Enterprise-oriented Brazilian provider with Tier III DCs and two-region replication; no independent price/performance benchmark located. The zero-egress claim is on the vendor's own page and uncontradicted, but there is no published price list PDF to cross-check the R$0.05 number against, so confidence on the exact rate is medium even though confidence on the egress policy is high.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: read broker, upstream_status 200 (final_url redirected to /produtos/storage). «Armazene grandes volumes por apenas R$0,05/GB»; «Sem Taxas — Zero Egress e API … a saída é gratuita, operações PUT, GET, LIST não pesam na fatura»
same page — «suporte a buckets de até 5PB e sem necessidade de provisionamento»; «Replicação em duas regiões distintas»; «imutabilidade WORM nativa»
search snippet — «Object Storage S3 | R$ 0,05/GB Sem Egress Fee … 50 TB | R$ 16.» (the 50 TB row was truncated in the snippet and not recoverable from the page body)

price_per_tb_month: $10.19/TB/mo at both 5 TB and 20 TB (strict per-GB, no tiers), egress $0. R$0.05/GB × 1024 GB/TB × 0.199082 USD/BRL = $10.19. Note this is per decimal GB on the vendor's wording; if billed per GiB the figure is $10.96/TB.
notes: R$0.05/GB/month, billed on stored GB only; buckets up to 5 PB, no provisioning. Positioned as «Armazenamento sem taxas de download (egress) ou API».

extras.agent_focus: Wave 7 cheap-PAID lane, regional angle: storage sold in RUB / CNY / BRL / INR / ZAR / TRY / PLN / UAH that never appears on Western price lists. Every paid candidate carries price_per_tb_month at USD-converted list price. FX fixed 2026-10-21 from open.er-api.com: RUB 82.5719/USD, CNY 6.6913, BRL 5.0231, INR 94.9952, ZAR 16.3972, TRY 49.5978, PLN 3.8923, UAH 45.0922, EUR 0.89075/USD. Excluded per brief: AWS, Azure, GCP, Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2. Headline result: the true regional floor with genuinely free egress is ~$2.00/TB/mo (Yandex 360 Profi 3 TB on a Russian card) rising to ~$4.17/TB/mo for the same product bought with a foreign card, and ~$5.95-7.56/TB/mo for flat-rate Western-facing file storage (TheHost, Rollin Host). Everything advertised below ~$2/TB/mo in this set is either capacity-capped, egress-metered, or unverifiable marketing.
